card.title: PANZER I DAK
card.text: Gets Shock when it moves into the frontline.
card.flavorText: The Panzer I was originally designed as a light training tank in the early 1930s, and its use in combat was limited due to its light armor and weak armaments (two 7.92mm MG13 machine guns). By the time the Afrika Korps was deployed to North Africa in 1941, the Panzer I was considered obsolete as a frontline combat vehicle. Some were converted into mobile artillery units by removing their turret. These mobile artillery units were called Panzerjäger I and equipped with various caliber heavy cannons and some were even used in an anti-tank role. However, a few Panzer I tanks were still used by the Deutsches Afrikakorps (DAK), primarily in a supporting role early in the campaign. These tanks were involved in reconnaissance missions, supply runs, and other non-frontline duties because their armor and firepower were inadequate for direct tank battles, especially against more powerful British and Allied tanks like the Matilda II. The Panzer I's light weight made it relatively mobile in the desert environment, but its combat effectiveness was very limited. It was soon replaced by more advanced tanks like the Panzer III and Panzer IV, which were far better suited to the rigors of desert warfare and the stronger Allied armor they faced.
